traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and technical requirements from docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md are fully implemented and verified:
- Rule Naming (REQ-RULE-NAME): The plugin exposes 'traceability/prefer-supports-annotation' as the primary rule name and 'traceability/prefer-implements-annotation' as a deprecated alias, wired in src/index.ts with meta.replacedBy and a deprecation note. Tests exercise both ruleIds in a single suite. - Optional Warning & Configurable Enforcement (REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING, REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY): The rule is not included in the recommended/strict presets, so it is disabled by default. Tests confirm it can be configured to 'warn' or 'error' for both rule names. When enabled, it emits recommendation diagnostics for legacy @story+@req usage. - Auto-fix Support & Single Story Conversion (REQ-AUTO-FIX, REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX): The implementation provides an ESLint fixer that transforms single-story comments consisting of one @story and one or more @req lines into a single @supports line with all REQ IDs, preserving the rest of the comment. Tests verify both single-req and multi-req transformations. - Multi-story Detection & Cannot-auto-fix Cases (REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT): The rule detects mixed @story/@req/@supports usage and multiple story paths, emits appropriate messages ('cannotAutoFix', 'multiStoryDetected'), and deliberately does not produce a fix. These behaviors are explicitly covered by tests. - Preserve Order / JSDoc Structure (REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT): The fixer logic carefully replaces only the @story line (with indentation preserved) and removes @req lines, leaving other JSDoc content and relative ordering intact. Documentation and tests confirm this behavior. - Both Formats Valid & Quality Standards (REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION, REQ-VALID-OUTPUT): With the rule off (default), only the core validation rules run, so legacy annotations remain fully valid. Even when enabled, comments with only @story, only @req, or only @supports are treated as valid. Auto-fix is conservative and only emits @supports when it can construct a valid single-story mapping; otherwise it warns without fixing, ensuring generated annotations pass existing @supports validation. - Documentation: Both the rule-specific doc (docs/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.md) and the migration guide (user-docs/migration-guide.md) describe the migration rule, its opt-in nature, configuration options, and concrete auto-fix examples, matching the story’s documentation acceptance criterion.
Targeted Jest tests for this story all pass, and the implementation and docs align closely with the specified behavior, so this story is assessed as PASSED.
